evidence.note: Runs run_tests.sh after essentially every meaningful kernel change, checking both correctness and cycle count before proceeding — solid anchor-5 loop discipline.
Builds a custom diagnostic script (test_schedule.py) to measure per-round scheduled bundle counts and test 16-set configs before applying — tighter cycle feedback than run_tests.sh provides.
Uses the custom harness to compare register-set configurations (16/20/28) and scheduler priority keys, doing per-configuration cycle attribution prior to committing changes into kernel.py.
Fixes RecursionError in dependency builder — reactive correctness fix, but caught via testing rather than an independent correctness harness.

Reasons about mathematical correctness of omitting wrap-around checks, but never builds differential testing vs the reference on custom inputs nor verifies slot-limit legality independently — correctness verification stays reliant on run_tests.sh.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds anchor-5: it runs run_tests.sh after every meaningful change (checking correctness and cycles) AND builds a custom diagnostic harness for per-round cycle measurement and configuration comparison — feedback beyond the provided tool. However it falls short of anchor-8 because that extra harness targets cycles/scheduling only; correctness is never independently verified via differential testing on custom inputs, sub-computation isolation, or independent slot-limit legality checks, remaining dependent on the single provided test's green run. This mix of strong cycle verification and standard correctness verification places it at a 6.
